clue.text: Dull, ordinary and unacceptable in sumo wrestling

indicators.note: in tells us the other letters sit inside the rearranged sumo
wrestling suggests the letters of sumo grappling and tumbling into a new order

parts.note: unacceptable is 'not on' in British idiom

explanation.surface: A spectator finds sumo wrestling tedious, commonplace and generally not acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrestling' makes MOUS, which the 'in' splits; 'not on' is British idiom for unacceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something monotonous never varies, which makes it boring, a close synonym of dull.

clue.text: Birds and marine mammals circling bottomless bay

indicators.note: circling means the mammals wrap around the other piece

parts.note: seals are marine mammals

indicators.note: bottomless removes the last letter, the bottom of a word in a down clue

parts.note: a gulf is a large bay

explanation.surface: A seaside scene: birds and seals going round and round a deep bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottomless' drops the final letter, the bottom of the word in a down entry, and 'circling' wraps the mammals round what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Seagulls are a familiar kind of seabird, so they are examples of birds.

clue.text: Cherishes a note about son

parts.note: do is a note of the sol-fa scale
re is Latin-derived 'about', as in business letters
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A parent treasures a brief message about their boy.
explanation.definitionFit: To adore someone is to love and treasure them dearly, which is to cherish them.

clue.text: Freezes chops daughter discarded

indicators.note: discarded says the daughter's letter is thrown out of the word

parts.note: to dice is to chop into cubes
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A cook freezes the chops after the daughter has thrown them out.
explanation.definitionFit: To ice something is to chill or turn it to ice, so ices is a synonym of freezes.

clue.text: Unruly crowd holds up South Carolina game

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece that holds up another sits beneath it, so the crowd comes after

parts.note: SC is the postal abbreviation for South Carolina
a rabble is a disorderly mob

explanation.surface: A riotous mob delays a sporting fixture in South Carolina.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrabble is a board game of building words from lettered tiles.

clue.text: Mindlessly repeat standard nonsense

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
rot is nonsense

explanation.surface: Someone thoughtlessly echoes the usual drivel.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot words is to echo them without understanding, as the talking bird does.

clue.text: Neither revolutionary supports independent press

indicators.note: in a down clue a supporting piece sits underneath, so it comes after
revolutionary means the word turns round, read backwards

parts.note: nor partners neither and stands for it here

explanation.surface: A newspaper that backs no revolutionaries supports a free press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' gives RON; in a down entry the piece that 'supports' sits underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: To iron clothes is to press them smooth with a hot iron.

clue.text: Resort hotel beside old abandoned vicarage

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: abandoned suggests the vicarage emptied of its contents, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A seaside resort's hotel stands next to a disused old vicarage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' empties VICARAGE to VE. HOVE is a seaside town on England's south coast, joined to Brighton.
explanation.definitionFit: Hove is an English seaside town, so it is an example of a resort.

clue.text: Spooner's European braves outdoor seating

indicators.note: Spooner's says the opening sounds of two words are swapped, in the manner of Reverend Spooner

parts.note: a Czech is a European
to brave a danger is to dare it

explanation.surface: A daring European faces up to the garden furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: CZECH DARES with the opening sounds swapped gives DECK CHAIRS; the swap works by sound, not spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Deckchairs are folding canvas chairs used outside, on beaches and lawns.

clue.text: Older woman's company? Flipping saucy stuff!

indicators.note: flipping means turning the word over, so it reads backwards

parts.note: ragu is an Italian meat sauce

explanation.surface: An older woman's companion exclaims about something cheeky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' turns RAGU into UGAR. 'Saucy stuff' plays on cheeky innuendo but means a pasta sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Cougar is slang for an older woman who seeks relationships with younger men.

clue.text: Hairstyle covered in elaborate nets for prom

indicators.note: covered in means the hairstyle is wrapped by the other letters
elaborate suggests the letters of nets are worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: an Afro is a bushy rounded hairstyle

explanation.surface: A big hairdo caught in fancy netting on the way to a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elaborate' makes SENT, split by 'covered in'. Prom is British for a seaside promenade, not only a school dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A prom, short for promenade, is the walkway along a seafront.

clue.text: Gangster's partners importing American-caught oysters, say

indicators.note: importing means taking the other letters in, inside the word

parts.note: a moll is a gangster's girlfriend
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Mob girlfriends smuggle in seafood caught in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Oysters are bivalve molluscs, so they are an example of the class, as 'say' signals.

clue.text: Be frugal with millions found in waste container

indicators.note: found in says the millions sit inside the container

parts.note: a skip is a large open bin for rubbish, in British use

explanation.surface: Someone thrifty with a fortune discovered in a dumpster.
explanation.walkthrough: A SKIP is the British word for a builder's dumpster.
explanation.definitionFit: To skimp is to spend or use too little, economising stingily.

clue.text: Pub outside Totnes regularly provides buffet

indicators.note: outside means the pub wraps around the other letters

parts.note: a bar is a pub

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of Totnes, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A pub on the edge of a Devon town lays on a spread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes TTE from Totnes, a town in Devon. 'buffet' is the verb, to strike, not a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: To buffet something is to strike it repeatedly, which is to batter it.

clue.text: They escape, sporting bits of pirate costumes

indicators.note: sporting, as in frolicking, has these letters played about with

explanation.surface: Fugitives slip away wearing parts of pirate outfits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sporting' looks like 'wearing' but signals the anagram of THEY ESCAPE.
explanation.definitionFit: Eye patches are worn by stage pirates as part of the classic outfit.

clue.text: Government department seconds fashion-conscious youths

parts.note: MOD is the Ministry of Defence, a British government department

explanation.surface: A ministry sends out style-minded youngsters in quick time.
explanation.walkthrough: Mods were a 1960s British youth subculture famous for sharp suits and scooters, and for clashes with rockers at Brighton.
explanation.definitionFit: Mods were stylish young people devoted to sharp clothing in 1960s Britain.

clue.text: Record Spinning Around, Free and It's a Sin

indicators.note: Around means the record's letters go round the other piece
spinning means the record turns round, its letters read backwards

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
to rid is to free

explanation.surface: A playlist of pop hits: Spinning Around, Free and It's a Sin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spinning' gives PE, which goes 'Around'. The surface names songs by Kylie Minogue and Pet Shop Boys; Pride is also a Brighton festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Pride is one of the seven deadly sins, so the clue's last words define it.

clue.text: Show about Henry and Mike's ghosts

indicators.note: about means the show wraps around the next piece

parts.note: a panto, short for pantomime, is a British Christmas stage show
H is the symbol for the henry, a unit of inductance
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet, and the 's gives S

explanation.surface: A stage production about Henry and Mike's spectral sightings.
explanation.walkthrough: A PANTO is a pantomime, the British family Christmas show with slapstick and audience participation.
explanation.definitionFit: Phantoms are spectres or apparitions, which is what ghosts are.

clue.text: Popular attraction run by tart

indicators.note: by means the run sits beside the tart, following it

parts.note: a tart is a kind of pie
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A crowd-pleaser operated by a pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: Brighton's Palace Pier is the theme's popular attraction.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaside pier, with its amusements and rides, is a crowd-drawing attraction.

clue.text: Eccentric VIP keeps a big cat in building

indicators.note: keeps means the scrambled letters hold the next piece inside them
eccentric suggests the letters of VIP behave oddly, rearranged

parts.note: a lion is a big cat

explanation.surface: An oddball celebrity houses a lion indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' rearranges VIP to PVI, which 'keeps' A to give PAVI. Brighton's Royal Pavilion is the theme's building.
explanation.definitionFit: A pavilion is a building, often ornamental, like Brighton's Royal Pavilion.

clue.text: Inconclusive test on Italy's Adriatic peninsula

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after, so the test comes second

parts.note: I is the international vehicle code for Italy, and the 's gives S

indicators.note: inconclusive means lacking a conclusion, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a trial is a test

explanation.surface: An unfinished examination of Italy's coastal peninsula.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inconclusive' cuts the last letter from TRIAL to leave TRIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Istria is a peninsula jutting into the Adriatic Sea, shared by Croatia, Slovenia and Italy.

clue.text: Ruler is somewhat sombre gentleman

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A monarch who is rather a gloomy fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: Brighton's Royal Pavilion was built for the Prince Regent.
explanation.definitionFit: A regent rules in place of a monarch who is too young, absent or unfit.

clue.text: South American scrambled up ravine

indicators.note: scrambled means these letters are jumbled, and also suits climbing

explanation.surface: A traveller from South America clambered up a gorge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrambled' reads as climbing but signals the anagram of UP RAVINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A Peruvian comes from Peru, a country in South America.

clue.text: Rest of class sit for photographer

parts.note: RE, religious education, is a school class in Britain
to pose is to sit for a photographer

explanation.surface: The rest of the pupils sit for their class photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rest of' reads as 'the remainder of', but 'Rest' alone is the definition. RE is religious education, a British school subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Repose is calm relaxation or sleep, a noun meaning rest.

clue.text: Bachelor woke 8's neighbour

parts.note: woke and 'right on' both describe someone socially and politically aware

explanation.surface: A single man roused the people next door.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 is HOVE, which sits directly beside Brighton on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Brighton and Hove adjoin each other and form one city, so Brighton is Hove's neighbour.

clue.text: Sweet sound of mythical bird

indicators.note: sound of says we want a word that is said like the bird's name

parts.note: the roc is a giant bird of Arabian legend

explanation.surface: The cry of a legendary bird is sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: ROCK is a hard British seaside stick of candy, often with the resort's name inside, as in Brighton rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock is a type of hard candy, so it is an example of a sweet.

clue.text: Boy raised on hospital food

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means sitting above, so the reversed boy comes first
raised means the word goes upwards, read backwards in a down clue

parts.note: a son is a boy
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A boy brought up on hospital meals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns SON upwards into NOS. NOSH is informal British slang for food.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosh is colloquial British for food or a meal.

clue.text: Posh Home Secretary left card

parts.note: PA is short for personal assistant, a secretary
an ace is a playing card

explanation.surface: A grand Home Secretary leaves a calling card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Home Secretary' looks like a single British cabinet job, but 'Posh Home' is the definition and 'Secretary' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A palace is a grand residence, the poshest kind of house.

clue.text: Spain broadcast sitcoms about working for financial experts

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the next piece
broadcast suggests the letters of sitcoms are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: on means working, as in a switched-on machine

explanation.surface: Spanish TV airs comedies about the working lives of money men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' makes COMISTS, which goes 'about' the working piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Economists study the economy and money, so they are experts in finance.

clue.text: Frank and Oscar exercise before noon

parts.note: O is Oscar in the NATO phonetic alphabet
PE is physical education, exercise

explanation.surface: Frank and Oscar work out before midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man's name beside Oscar but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone open is candid and honest, which is what being frank means.
